problem: The formula is written as P(xᵢ = v | C), but for a numeric feature a normal density is not a probability of the value v; it is a density. A student can read this as an ordinary probability and wonder why values above 1 appear.
fix: Add one short line: 'This is a density, not a probability; densities above 1 are normal, and only the comparison across classes matters.'

problem: score(C) ÷ Σ score(C′) is presented with ≈ and called 'not a guarantee of true probability'. Under the independence assumption this division is exactly the model's posterior; it is only approximate as a description of the real world. The wording blurs the two ideas.
fix: Say: 'Dividing by the sum gives the model's posterior exactly; it is only approximate as a real-world probability because the independence assumption is not true.'

problem: The pointer to chapter 3.5 is plain text, so it does not work as a cross-chapter link in the book.
fix: Write it as a link: 3.5 Bayesian belief networks.

problem: The caption says the values shown match the six-day worked example, but the graph shows only the prior note P(Yes)=4/6; no conditional table values (CPTs) appear. The claim is not true of the figure as drawn.
fix: Say: 'The graph shows the structure and the class prior 4/6 used in the six-day worked example; the conditional tables are computed in the example.'

problem: The answer says α controls how much probability is added to every feature value. In the formula α is added to the counts, not to the probabilities; the probability change is a result of smoothing.
fix: Say: 'α is added to every count (and αV to the class count in the denominator). Larger α pulls the conditionals toward uniform; α = 0 means no smoothing.'
